angle: new_interface_method on a 12-method index cache interface — 3 named implementations in the indexcache package PLUS one hidden noopCache struct buried in the storegateway consumer package
difficulty_notes: The IndexCache interface has 12 existing methods. Models must scan all four concrete implementations: InMemoryIndexCache and RemoteIndexCache are obvious (in the same package as the interface). TracingIndexCache is less obvious (a decorator wrapper also in the same package). The critical trap is noopCache in pkg/storegateway/bucket.go — it is a private struct defined far from the interface definition, in a consumer package, implementing all 12 IndexCache methods as single-line stubs. Models that do text-search-based discovery (searching for the interface name) will find noopCache easily; models that reason structurally ('where are the implementations?') will look only in the indexcache package and miss it. The interface is also used as a field type in bucket.go and bucket_stores.go — these are call sites, not implementations, so they do not fail to compile.
